name: Chinese fir (杉木, Cunninghamia lanceolata)
summary: The most important fast-growing timber of southern China: pale, light, soft, easily worked and resistant to insects. In Chenghuai it is the purlins, rafters and roof boards, painted the same iron-oxide red as the columns and darkened by age and smoke.

class.text: Conifer (Cupressaceae); wood pale yellow to white, soft but durable, easily worked, resistant to insects and termites.
class.source: Earle, C.J. (ed.) The Gymnosperm Database: Cunninghamia lanceolata, last modified 2026-07-30, https://www.conifers.org/cu/Cunninghamia_lanceolata.php

whyAnAccent.text: Principle 2 names one oak. Chenghuai is built as it would be in Beijing, and its approved Materials board names Korean pine, Chinese fir and plantation Phoebe. Each is declared an accent of the oak family (D-014): timber in the oak's role, tied to it by value and hue under its finish. The Architect may overturn this reading.
whyAnAccent.source: MuseeVision/Journal/Decisions.md, D-014 (Matter: every substance carries its family; an accent names its core family); plan/proposals/chenghuai/canvas/Materials.dc.html (approved Chenghuai proposal: '營造')

formation.how: A conifer of the warm regions south of the Chang Jiang, grown in plantations from seed, cuttings or suckers (rare among conifers). Its light, straight timber has long been used for houses, bridges, ships and coffins.
